messages.author: f76413c32828a961
messages.subject: Question about ddply
parts:
Hi there,

I am trying out the plyr package and the codes from the ggplot book.

When I submit the following to select the smallest by color group:
ddply(diamonds, .(color), subset, carat == min(carat))

The results for color=="D" are:
carat cut color clarity depth table price x y
z
1 0.20 Ideal D VS2 61.5 57 367 3.81 3.77 2.33
2 0.20 Premium D VS2 62.3 60 367 3.73 3.68 2.31
3 0.20 Premium D VS2 61.7 60 367 3.77 3.72 2.31

That I understand. So when I submitted the following:
ddply(diamonds, .(color), subset, order(carat) <= 2)

The results for color=="D" are:
carat cut color clarity depth table price x y z
1 0.30 Ideal D SI1 62.1 56 552 4.30 4.33 2.68
2 0.24 Very Good D VVS1 61.5 60 553 3.97 4.00 2.45

I thought the second command is supposed to extract the two smallest
diamonds of color "D" which are both 0.2 carat from the first
command. Can anyone explain why?

Sorry for the silly question. It looks like something very simple but
I just didn't get it. Thanks!!!

Kel

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Question about ddply
parts:
Hi

probably what you want is rank(), not order(). try

ddply(diamonds, .(color), subset, rank(carat,ties.method="first") <= 2)

and see
?order
?rank
